response_json.MatterTitle: F/S Amending the Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan to Incorporate Certain Growth and Development Principles Arising Out of the Planned Growth Strategy (Cadigan)
response_json.MatterEXText1:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\qj\fs22 R-02-112 proposes text and policy amendments to the Albuquerque-Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan.  The proposed amendments derive from an extensive, comprehensive and integrated study of existing conditions, trends, costs and benefits, sustainability, environmental and social inequities, policy, regulatory and institutional disconnects.  In addition, the study was done over several years with a great deal of public input, and was aided by the contributions of several professional consultants.
\par 
\par The proposed amendments respond to a variety of concerns expressed by the public and local elected officials with regard to the environment, fiscal, economic, and social consequences of metropolitan growth.  In addition, local elected officials and other public interests have expressed concern in numerous forums that the existing City-County Comprehensive Plan and implementation tools and practices in use are not a fully effective growth management system.
\par 
\par The proposed amendments would integrate these policy directions into the existing Comprehensive Plan, including PGS findings and recommendations that growth in population, housing and jobs be more thoughtfully distributed in order to make the metropolitan area more sustainable environmentally, economically, socially and fiscally.  The amendments also reinforce the Comprehensive Plan's emphasis on maintaining the existing community and its vitality, on better locating jobs and housing relative to basic needs and each other, on efficient use of public resources and infrastructure, on recognizing the importance of mixed land use activity centers and multi-modal transportation development and of correcting public infrastructure rehabilitation needs and deficiencies in existing neighborhoods.
\par 
\par The bill includes the following policies that would be included into the Comprehensive Plan.  Policy A deals with the infrastructure and growth plan, stating that it should guide urban growth and development of the Albuquerque/Bernalillo County area.  Policy B emphasizes the importance of the existing community and states that it will be a priority in terms of policies, development regulations, economic development, service delivery, and public expenditures.  Policy C states that neighborhoods should be diverse, have close proximity to activity and employment centers, a mix of housing types, basic needs and civic facilities, as well as being pedestrian and transit and bicycle friendly.  Policy D states that the diverse neighborhoods should have ongoing improvement, socially, economically, and in their built environment, that growth should have positive impact on residents' lives.  Policy E deals with public resources to correct the deficiencies and rehabilitation needs.  Policy F addresses new growth and the fact that it should be adequately served with infrastructure before it's allowed to occur.  Policy G deals with preservation, vistas, open space, and urban growth that's harmonious with the natural environment.  Policy H deals with the efficient provision of capital facilities and preservation of existing neighborhoods and businesses.
\par 
\par The original bill was submitted to the City Planning Department for review by the Environmental Planning Commission (EPC).  The Planning Department made revisions to the original bill and submitted it to the EPC for their review.  The EPC recommended approval based on several findings.  Their recommendations to the revised bill were incorporated into a floor substitute and forwarded to the City Council.  No opposition was raised to the proposed bill or to any of the findings at the EPC hearing.  At their April 14th meeting, the City Council received the floor substitute and referred it to the Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Government Commission (ABCGC) for their review.  The ABCGC recommended that the County Planning Commission review the floor substitute before the Board of County Commissioners review the bill.
\par }
